Campaign angle notes:

- Four angles are legally approved: price cut (A), quality story (B), limited-time urgency (C), customer testimonial (D).
- Analytics reported 2/5 pushes landed after Day 5 and 3/5 after Day 10. No per-day or angle-level breakdown is available, so do not attribute wins confidently to a specific angle.
- Quality story (B) and customer testimonial (D) were used most often and are reasonable trust/value-focused defaults, but their relative performance is unproven.
- Limited-time urgency (C) was tried once with no isolatable result; avoid assuming the Saturday context improves urgency performance.
- Price cut (A) was not tested in the recorded period, so its effectiveness is unknown.
- Support-reported unsubscribes were processed but provide insufficient evidence to change angle strategy.
- No deliverability complaints were reported.
- New signups and refreshed creative are contextual signals, not evidence that a particular angle will perform better.
- Continue testing deliberately and seek angle-level reporting before making strong optimization decisions.

Campaign angle notes:

- Four angles remain legally approved: price cut (A), quality story (B), limited-time urgency (C), and customer testimonial (D).
- Analytics reports are pooled summaries only: prior reports showed 2/5 pushes landing after Day 5 and 3/5 after Day 10; later reports showed 1/5 after Day 15 and 2/5 after Day 20. There is no per-day, angle-level, or creative-level breakdown.
- Recent pushes used B on Days 11–12, 14, 17–18, and 20; A on Days 13, 15–16, and 19. This still does not establish that either angle performs better.
- B and D remain reasonable trust/value-focused defaults, but B’s frequent use and the Day 20 pooled result (2/5) are not evidence of B effectiveness. A was previously untested; its recent use is exploratory, not conclusive.
- C was tried once with no isolatable result. Saturday timing does not establish an advantage for urgency.
- D has not produced an isolatable result in the available reports.
- Refreshed banner art occurred alongside several pushes, but no creative-level attribution is available.
- New signups and support-reported unsubscribes (processed) are contextual signals, not sufficient grounds to change angle strategy.
- No deliverability complaints have been reported.
- Continue deliberate rotation/testing. Seek angle- and creative-level reporting before making optimization claims; interpret all pooled results as exploratory.

Campaign angle notes:

- All four angles remain legally approved: price cut (A), quality story (B), limited-time urgency (C), and customer testimonial (D).
- Analytics provides only pooled summaries, with no per-day, angle-level, or creative-level attribution. Historical reports: 2/5 after Day 5, 3/5 after Day 10, 1/5 after Day 15, 2/5 after Day 20, 3/5 after Day 25, and 4/5 after Day 30. These results are exploratory and cannot establish angle performance.
- Recent usage: B on Days 11–12, 14, 17–18, and 20; A on Days 13, 15–16, and 19; D on Days 21–30 consecutively. D’s pooled-period results (3/5 and 4/5) do not demonstrate that D caused the improvement, and D is now overused relative to the other angles.
- B and D remain reasonable trust/value-focused options, but neither has an isolatable result. A remains exploratory. C has only one unisolatable test; Saturday timing does not prove urgency performs better.
- Refreshed banner art coincided with multiple pushes, including during D usage; no creative-level attribution is available. Do not infer banner or angle effectiveness from pooled results.
- New signups, processed support-reported unsubscribes, and absence of deliverability complaints are contextual signals only; they do not justify changing angle strategy.
- Resume deliberate rotation across A, B, C, and D rather than continuing D. Seek angle-, day-, and creative-level reporting before making optimization claims.

Campaign angle notes:

- All four angles remain legally approved: price cut (A), quality story (B), limited-time urgency (C), and customer testimonial (D).
- Analytics provides only pooled summaries, with no reliable per-day, angle-level, or creative-level attribution. Historical reports: 2/5 after Day 5, 3/5 after Day 10, 1/5 after Day 15, 2/5 after Day 20, 3/5 after Day 25, and 4/5 after Day 30. These cannot establish angle performance.
- D was used consecutively on Days 21–30 and is overused; its pooled results do not show causation.
- C was then used consecutively on Days 31–40, including both banner-refresh events. Analytics reported 0/5 for the latest pooled period, but no per-day breakdown is available, so this is a cautionary signal—not proof that C caused the outcome. Do not continue treating repeated C use as a clean test.
- B and D remain reasonable trust/value options; A remains exploratory. C has now had extended recent exposure but still lacks isolatable attribution. Saturday timing does not establish urgency effectiveness.
- Refreshed banner art coincided with multiple pushes, including C usage. Do not infer banner or angle effectiveness without creative-level reporting.
- Signups, processed support-reported unsubscribes, and lack of deliverability complaints are contextual signals only; they do not justify angle changes or performance claims.
- Resume deliberate rotation across A, B, C, and D rather than repeating one angle. Request angle-, day-, and creative-level reporting before optimization decisions.

Campaign angle notes:

- All four angles remain legally approved: price cut (A), quality story (B), limited-time urgency (C), and customer testimonial (D).
- Analytics provides only pooled summaries, with no reliable per-day, angle-level, or creative-level attribution. Historical pooled results (including 4/5 and later 2/5 periods) cannot establish angle performance.
- D was used consecutively on Days 21–30 and remains overused; its pooled results do not show causation.
- C was used consecutively on Days 31–40, including both banner-refresh events. The latest pooled period reported 0/5, but this is only a cautionary signal, not proof against C. Do not treat repeated C use as a clean test.
- A was then used on most pushes from Days 41–45 and 47–50, with one B push on Day 46. Pooled results of 4/5 and later 2/5 do not demonstrate A effectiveness. A is now also overused and should not be repeated as evidence-driven optimization.
- B and D remain reasonable trust/value options; A and C are exploratory until attribution improves. Rotate deliberately across all four rather than favoring A or repeating any single angle.
- Refreshed banner art coincided with multiple pushes, including A and prior C usage. Do not infer banner or angle effectiveness without creative-level reporting.
- Saturday timing, signups, processed support-reported unsubscribes, and lack of deliverability complaints are contextual only; they do not justify angle changes or performance claims.
- Request angle-, day-, and creative-level reporting before making optimization decisions. Treat all recent outcomes as unattributable until then.

Campaign angle notes:

- All four angles remain legally approved: A price cut, B quality story, C limited-time urgency, D customer testimonial.
- Analytics still provides only pooled summaries; no reliable per-day, angle-level, or creative-level attribution. Recent pooled results (B: 2/5, then 4/5) do not establish that B caused performance.
- B was used on every push from Days 51–60 and is now overused. Do not repeat B as an evidence-driven optimization; rotate deliberately to another approved angle.
- A was heavily used on Days 41–45 and 47–50 and remains overused. C was used consecutively on Days 31–40, including banner refreshes; its 0/5 pooled period is only a cautionary signal, not proof against C. D was overused on Days 21–30.
- Since each angle has now had substantial or repeated exposure, choose among A/C/D based on deliberate rotation and campaign needs, not claimed performance. Avoid favoring any angle until attribution improves.
- Refreshed banner art coincided with multiple pushes, including B on Days 52, 56, and 60. Do not claim or infer that the refresh improved results without creative-level reporting.
- Send timing, signups, processed support-reported unsubscribes, and absence of deliverability complaints are contextual only; they do not justify angle changes or performance claims.
- Continue requesting angle-, day-, and creative-level reporting. Treat pooled outcomes as unattributable and avoid unsupported causal claims.
